transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (NovaEdge Partnerships), Tom Hsu (NovaEdge Product), Ravi Patel (NovaEdge Infra)

Summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and NovaEdge to explore channel/resell partnership and technical integration options (private deployments, dedicated GPU pools, and joint benchmark/pilot). Discussed NovaEdge's infra, typical customer profiles, security/compliance needs, and initial pilot scope. Agreed on follow-ups: deck + SOC2, technical deep-dive, and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Emily (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Emily from Redwood, AE on the partnership side. Marco from our SE team is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Lena (NovaEdge): Good, thanks Emily. Excited to chat - I'm Lena, I lead partnerships at NovaEdge.
[00:16] Tom (NovaEdge): Tom here, head of product. Quick heads-up we have Ravi from infra who will ask the nerd questions.
[00:23] Ravi (NovaEdge): Hi all.
[00:25] Marco (Redwood): Great, thanks. Quick agenda: intros, high-level Redwood product + partner motion, NovaEdge infra and go-to-market fit, technical constraints (VPC/peering/KMS), and propose next steps.
[00:40] Emily: We'll keep it flexible, mostly Q&A. Marco, do you want to give 3 minute overview?
[00:45] Marco: Sure. Redwood is a dev-first inference platform — we do hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployments into VPCs or on-prem for regulated customers. Focus is production performance: latency, throughput, cost. We also have an Optimize toolkit for batching, quant recommendations, and per-route observability.
[01:10] Tom: When you say "dedicated", is that multi-tenant or single-tenant GPU pools?
[01:16] Marco: Dedicated means reserved GPU pools isolated per customer; can be single-tenant nodes in a pool. For partners, we often talk about either co-hosted models or resell of Dedicated capacity; depends on commercial terms.
[01:28] Lena: NovaEdge is a hardware + cloud integrator — we sell racks to hyperscale and offer GPU-backed cloud regions. We're exploring partnerships to offer turnkey LLM inference as a managed add-on. Typical customers are enterprise ISVs and labs who want low-latency inference close to their VPC.
[01:45] Emily: That aligns — lots of customers want private deployments or Dedicated with VPC peering. Quick question: what GPU SKUs are you running and which clouds/regions?
[01:58] Ravi: We run a mix: A100 80GB in our high-perf region, H100 in some new clusters, and our next-gen NovaEdge X (custom) which is Ampere-based. Regions: US-west, EU-central, and a Singapore edge.
[02:15] Marco: Cool, H100 and A100 are good for common open models. For custom SKUs, we usually evaluate kernel support and quant paths. There can be subtle perf differences if GPU architecture deviates.
[02:30] Tom: How much work is model onboarding for you? Like if we wanted to ship Model X as a validated variant on NovaEdge, what's the cycle?
[02:38] Marco: Depends on model size and if there's custom ops. Typical onboarding 2-3 sprints to validate kernels, quantize to int8/bf16, run latency/throughput benchmarks. For partners we provide a validation playbook and can co-run a pilot.
[02:55] Lena: On commercial side, we want simple partner tiers: referral, reseller, and managed service. Can Redwood support reseller pricing and partner-managed deployment?
[03:06] Emily: Yes, we have partner programs. We can support reseller flows and provide a partner console for usage reporting. We'll send the partner deck and sample contract language.
[03:18] Ravi: On security — most of our customers require SOC2 + SAML SSO, and some need HSM/KMS for keys. How do you handle keys and audit logs?
[03:28] Marco: We support customer-managed KMS (via AWS KMS or external HSM) for private deployments and can provide detailed audit logs. Our control plane can be private for Private customers. We'll share a SOC2 and a network diagram. Transcription note: sometimes "K V M S" or "K V cash" in old exports, so please ignore typos.
[03:52] Tom: Latency expectations — certain customers want sub-50ms for small prompts. Can you achieve that on dedicated infra?
[03:59] Marco: Sub-50ms is realistic for smaller models on optimized kernels with batching tuned. For large LLMs at scale, we typically aim for SLOs like p95 under 200-400ms depending on model. We use continuous batching and prefix/KV cache to reduce token cost and latency.
[04:20] Ravi: Do you do our routing? Like can requests be routed by policy to cheaper region or fallback models?
[04:28] Marco: Yes — smart routing by policy (latency, cost, region, tier) and automated fallback to quantized or smaller model variants if capacity constrained. Good for graceful degradation.
[04:40] Lena: Can we co-market? We'd want joint case studies for any managed deployment wins.
[04:45] Emily: Absolutely — partner marketing is part of the program.
[04:48] Tom: On the technical pilot — what's the minimum scope you'd need from us to run a benchmark?
[04:54] Marco: We'd like: (1) infra spec (GPU type, network egress/cap), (2) a representative model or list (model name + size), (3) sample prompt set or dataset, and (4) target SLOs (latency/throughput/cost per token). That allows us to propose a benchmarking matrix.
[05:12] Ravi: We'll need to confirm network peering options — some customers want direct VPC peering, some use private interconnect. Do you support peering and private control plane?
[05:22] Marco: Yes, Private deployments support VPC peering and a private control plane with customer-managed networking. On-prem also possible for air-gapped customers.
[05:31] Lena: From a GTM perspective, we sell both infra and managed software. Do you have partner enablement docs?
[05:37] Emily: We'll include partner enablement in the deck and a partner portal link in the follow-up.
[05:42] Tom: Any friction points for onboarding customers that we should be aware of?
[05:47] Marco: Typical friction: network setup (firewall rules, peering), KMS integration timelines, and model ops (large weight transfers and quantization). We try to provide a runbook. Also, some OSS models need kernel-level tuning for best perf on nonstandard GPUs.
[06:05] Ravi: Weight transfer — for large models, are you doing model hosting in place or do we push weights to Redwood?
[06:12] Marco: For Private deployment, weights can live in your storage and we deploy runtime within your VPC; for hosted API you upload or we host depending on agreement. For reseller/partner-managed flows we commonly do private control plane with customer-managed storage.
[06:27] Lena: Curious about billing — do you offer committed reserved pools like monthly commits?
[06:33] Emily: Yes, Redwood Dedicated offers reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits and autoscaling policies + burst. Partner billing models can be arranged.
[06:40] Tom: On observability — we need token-level cost and latency breakdown per route.
[06:46] Marco: That's in the Console — route/model dashboards, tracing and per-token cost breakdowns. You can expose those to customers or partners depending on role/permissions.
[06:58] Ravi: Do you support RBAC and SAML so our ops team can have limited visibility?
[07:03] Marco: Yes, SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported.
[07:07] Emily: Quick interjection, previous customers used Redwood as a backend for a managed inference product; partners either resell Dedicated or embed our runtime in partner-managed on-prem stacks.
[07:18] Lena: On commercial margins, high level, is there room for partner margin on resell and managed services?
[07:24] Emily: We typically structure reseller discounts and channel margins. We'll surface examples in the deck.
[07:30] Tom: Anything about model licensing? If the customer wants a commercial LLM, are there additional steps?
[07:35] Marco: Yes, model licensing can be separate — for open models we handle runtime; for commercial models like XXX you'd need licensing from model vendor. We advise customers on compatible variants.
[07:47] Ravi: For benchmarks, we care about throughput when batching many concurrent requests. Does Redwood support continuous batching?
[07:54] Marco: Yep — continuous batching and smart scheduling are core features. You can tune batch window vs latency tradeoffs. Optimize suggests batch configs based on workload.
[08:05] Lena: From a partnership ops standpoint, can we get a sandbox account to demo to customers?
[08:10] Emily: Yes, we provide sandbox credits and a quickstart. We'll include access info in the follow-up.
[08:15] Tom: Any past reference partners doing this?
[08:19] Emily: We have a few system integrator partners and a hardware partner; I'll share anonymized case studies.
[08:24] Ravi: Networking — do you support granular subnet control and egress restrictions? Some regulated customers require strict egress policies.
[08:33] Marco: Private deployments are customer-controlled so you can lock down egress. We also support VPC endpoints in many clouds.
[08:40] Tom: Are there any performance regs with the NovaEdge X SKU? We've seen some frameworks need kernel work.
[08:46] Marco: We evaluate kernel compatibility as part of onboarding. If custom SKUs use uncommon instruction sets, we may need a custom kernel build or fall back to compatible codepaths that might affect perf. That becomes part of the validation work.
[08:59] Lena: Let's talk pilot structure — what's a minimal pilot for us to validate partner flow?
[09:04] Marco: Minimal pilot: deploy Redwood runtime in your test VPC or run a lightweight benchmark on one of your clusters; validate model inference correctness, measure latency/throughput for target prompts; test routing/fallback; verify security (KMS/SAML). Typical pilot length 2-4 weeks.
[09:20] Tom: Any pitfalls in the first two weeks?
[09:23] Marco: Often network and key provisioning take the longest. Plan that early. Also model weight transfer and quantization tuning.
[09:32] Ravi: For telemetry, do you stream logs to our SIEM?
[09:36] Marco: Yes — we can forward logs to your SIEM and support audit log ingestion.
[09:40] Lena: Questions from our side: partner margin, enablement timeline, and support SLAs for managed installs.
[09:48] Emily: We'll outline tiers: referral, reseller, and managed service with corresponding enablement, SLAs, and support packages in the deck.
[09:55] Tom: Can we get an example SOW for a 3-week pilot?
[09:59] Emily: Yes, we'll include a pilot SOW template.
[10:02] Marco: For benchmarks, suggest we start with a small LLM (7B) and a mid-size (30-70B) to cover the spectrum. That gives a sense of latency and scaling.
[10:12] Ravi: We'll provide a dataset and traffic pattern — maybe 60/40 short prompts vs long context.
[10:18] Marco: Perfect. Also helpful: expected concurrency and p95 targets.
[10:22] Lena: On legal/compliance — anything that typically causes delays?
[10:26] Emily: Data residency and contractual security clauses sometimes add time. We'll pull our standard security pack (SOC2, penetration test summary) and share.
[10:34] Tom: For channel ops, do you have co-branded consoles or white-label options?
[10:38] Emily: There's some co-branding for partner portals; we can discuss white-label on larger deals.
[10:43] Ravi: Let's get into a few clarifying tech items — Marco, how do you implement KV cache? Is it sharded or local?
[10:50] Marco: Our KV cache is per instance and we manage distributed cache for prefix caching — we can configure TTLs, and for private deployments it sits behind your network. Sometimes transcripts show "K V cash" typo, ha.
[11:03] Tom: You mentioned quantization recommendations — do you have automated toolchain?
[11:07] Marco: We have an Optimize toolkit that recommends quant / kernel profiles based on workload; for partners we often run recommended profiles then fine-tune.
[11:16] Emily: Quick ask for everyone: who should be the operational point for NovaEdge?
[11:20] Lena: Ravi will be the ops lead. I'll be partner PM. Tom will handle product-level decisions.
[11:27] Ravi: Great. I'll upload infra spec and preferred sample dataset.
[11:31] Marco: Fantastic — we'll draft a benchmark plan.
[11:33] Lena: Commercial question — if a NovaEdge customer wants a fully managed Redwood private deployment, do you have a partner revenue share?
[11:40] Emily: Yes — partner revenue share can be structured; we'll include an example comp table.
[11:44] Tom: For early pilots, we'd like to get an NDA and maybe some mutual NDAs in place.
[11:49] Emily: We have an NDA template; I'll send it.
[11:52] Ravi: A few infra specifics: our peering supports BGP and Direct Connect equivalents, and we can provision private L3 peering in the density regions. Any issues with that?
[12:03] Marco: That's fine — supports standard peering models. We'll need firewall rules and ports; we'll share runbook.
[12:10] Lena: Timeline question: we want to launch a joint offering H2 2026 if pilot goes well. Realistic?
[12:18] Emily: Yes, H2 2026 is aggressive but feasible with a 2-3 month pilot + enablement and two initial customer wins.
[12:26] Tom: Any immediate blockers from Redwood's side?
[12:30] Marco: None; just need infra spec, model list and access arrangement to run benchmarks.
[12:35] Emily: We'll send deck, pilot SOW, SOC2, and a pilot S3 endpoint or sandbox creds.
[12:42] Lena: Great.
[12:44] [Longer discussion about billing cadence and partner margins, some cross-talk]
[20:10] Marco: Quick note — for cost optimization at scale, we recommend quantization and autoscaling with burst policy. Our Optimize tool can suggest target settings.
[20:22] Ravi: When you say autoscaling, do you support scheduled scaling?
[20:26] Marco: Yes scheduled and policy-based.
[20:29] Tom: Are there any penalties for burst beyond committed capacity?
[20:33] Emily: We typically allow a burst buffer but it depends on contract. We'll include an example.
[20:38] Marco: Also fallback to regional cheaper model variants helps keep SLAs.
[20:42] Lena: For joint GTM we'd like a partner playbook.
[20:46] Emily: We'll include a 1-pager partner playbook in the follow-up.
[20:50] [Noise/overlap] Speaker attribution imperfect here.
[30:05] Marco: On orchestration: we support pinned model versions and rollouts (canary/A-B) so you can roll new model variants safely.
[30:15] Ravi: That matters for customers who want strict reproducibility.
[30:18] Marco: Exactly. And we expose rollout APIs.
[30:22] Tom: Anything else on ops?
[30:25] Marco: We'll also include tracing hooks and sampling for debugging regressions.
[30:32] Lena: Final commercial question — partner enablement cost?
[30:36] Emily: Usually included in reseller agreement up to a point; premium enablement and white-labelling may have fees.
[30:42] [Wrap-up section]
[31:00] Emily: OK let's recap: action items — Emily will send partner deck, SOC2, NDA and pilot SOW; Marco will draft benchmark plan; Ravi will send infra spec and sample dataset; we'll schedule an SE deep-dive next week. Is that accurate?
[31:16] Ravi: Yes.
[31:18] Lena: Yep.
[31:20] Tom: Sounds good.
[31:22] Emily: I'll follow up with proposed times for the deep dive. Anything else from NovaEdge?
[31:28] Lena: No, thanks everyone.
[31:31] Tom: Not from me.
[31:33] Ravi: All good.
[31:35] Emily: Great, we'll send the materials. Thanks all.
[31:40] [Meeting ends with small pleasantries and a couple seconds of crosstalk]

Recap (auto-summary):
- Partnership fit looks promising: NovaEdge provides GPU-backed cloud/edge and wants to offer Redwood inference as managed add-on or reseller flow.
- Technical alignment: GPUs (A100/H100/NovaEdge X) are supported but will require onboarding/validation for custom SKUs.
- Security: NovaEdge needs SOC2, SAML, KMS/HSM support — Redwood supports these for Private deployments.
- Pilot: 2-4 week pilot to validate perf and security. Next steps as listed above.

References/links mentioned: partner deck (will be shared), pilot SOW template (will be shared), Redwood partner portal (link will be provided in follow-up).

End of transcript.
